clue.text: Party over, that fellow and the writer will make for opera

parts.note: Lab is the short form of the Labour Party
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a male person referred to is he
the writer of the clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A celebration ends, and a man and the author together will go off to see an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's La Bohème is one of the best-known works in the operatic repertoire, so it is an example.

clue.text: Take position over Schubertian article or multiple Schubertian articles

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to lie is to take up a position, as a thing lies in place
der is a German definite article, the language Schubert wrote in

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stance on a piece by Schubert, or on several of his works.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'articles' in the definition are songs, not grammar: lieder is the plural of lied, a German art song like Schubert's.
explanation.definitionFit: Schubert wrote hundreds of German art songs, so the songs are his works in the plural.

clue.text: Incitement to war: assault involving 50, then 100

indicators.note: then says the assault next takes in the hundred numeral as well
the assault word takes in the fifty numeral

parts.note: battery is the legal term for physical assault
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A rousing call to arms: an attack with fifty troops, followed by a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: BATTERY takes in L and then C, at different points.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle cry is a shout raised to rally troops in combat, so it urges men to fight.

clue.text: Curtailed search risked overlooking a county area

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to hunt is to search

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so the letter is skipped

parts.note: dared means ventured or risked

explanation.surface: A brief search that took chances missed part of a county.
explanation.walkthrough: A hundred was an old English subdivision of a county.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically English counties were split into administrative districts called hundreds, each a part of the shire.

clue.text: Setter's view depends on this? I don't believe it

definitions.meaning: the setter, speaking of their own eye, sees through it, so their view relies on it

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker's opinion rests on something that is frankly incredible.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'my eye' dismisses a claim as nonsense, an idiomatic expression of scepticism.

clue.text: Biting currents one repeatedly dives into

indicators.note: repeatedly says the numeral goes in a second time, one into each current
something diving into water goes inside it, so the numeral is put inside the currents

parts.note: AC and DC are the two kinds of electrical current, alternating and direct
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone keeps plunging into cold, sharp-edged flowing water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dives into' puts I into AC and 'repeatedly' puts a second I into DC: AC-I and D-I-C.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting remark is sharp and caustic, just as an acidic comment stings with sourness.

clue.text: Scoundrel quiet about independent source of yellow dye

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a scoundrel

indicators.note: about means the quiet word goes round the letter

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum

explanation.surface: A rogue keeps quiet about where an independent supplier gets yellow colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadmium compounds give the pigment cadmium yellow, so the metal is where that colour comes from.

clue.text: No front-line soldiers hit the bottle

parts.note: lines labelled alphabetically run A, B, C, D; D is a rear line, not the front one
a rank is a line of soldiers standing side by side

explanation.surface: Troops who were not in the front line took to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Not the A rank at the front but a rank further back: the D rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the bottle is to drink alcohol heavily, so it is an idiom for drinking.

clue.text: Repair includes care for headless puppet

indicators.note: the remedy word holds the shortened care word inside it

parts.note: to cure is to remedy or put right

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: to treat a patient is to care for them

explanation.surface: Mending a puppet that has lost its head takes some care.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature can mean someone wholly controlled by another, a tool or puppet of a patron.

clue.text: Prisoner heading for that bar, providing evidence of flight

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: A convict making for the bar leaves signs that he has escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests the prisoner escaping; it means an aircraft's flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrail is the vapour trail left in the sky by a jet, showing where an aircraft passed.

clue.text: Deviously enter election with a Democrat breaking this international agreement

indicators.note: a devious route twists and turns, so the letters are rearranged
the extra letters break into the jumbled words, joining the mix

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Democrat cheats their way into a poll, wrecking a treaty between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deviously' and 'breaking' together signal that ENTER, ELECTION, A and D are mixed up as one pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 understanding between Britain and France, a diplomatic pact between states.

clue.text: Amplify a lot of stuff presented in two forms of English

indicators.note: the shortened word is set inside the pair of abbreviations

parts.note: ENG and E are both standard abbreviations for English

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to lard is to stuff or fill, as when larding meat or a speech

explanation.surface: Someone makes a lot of material bigger by giving it in two versions of the language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' is a verb here, to lard; 'a lot of' drops its final letter and 'presented in' sets the rest between two abbreviations for English.
explanation.definitionFit: To amplify something is to make it bigger or fuller, which is to expand or magnify it.

clue.text: Country fellow cutting into odd parts of twenty trees

indicators.note: the rustic cuts into the selected letters, splitting them
the odd-numbered letters of the word are taken, first, third and fifth

parts.note: a hick is an unsophisticated rustic, a country bumpkin

explanation.surface: A yokel pushes his way through a scattering of trees, twenty of them perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd parts of' twenty gives TET, which HICK cuts into.
explanation.definitionFit: A thicket is a dense growth of shrubs and small trees, so the plural noun fits the clump.

clue.text: University and so on backed intended answers defending copyright

indicators.note: backed means the whole string is read from back to front

parts.note: what you intended is what you aimed at

indicators.note: the pair of answers surrounds the copyright mark as if guarding it

parts.note: A is the usual abbreviation for answer, so two answers give AA
C is the abbreviation for copyright, as in the circled C symbol

explanation.surface: Universities and similar places hold to their target answers while protecting their copyright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defending' puts C between the two A's; then 'backed' turns AIMED+ACA round.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholarly institutions collectively, hence a university and others like it.

clue.text: Bloomer made by a doctor in Welsh town

indicators.note: the article and the tampering word sit inside the town name

parts.note: Mold is a town in north-east Wales
to rig is to doctor or tamper with

explanation.surface: A doctor in a Welsh town makes an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A marigold is a flowering plant, so in crossword terms something that blooms.

clue.text: Vicar not in, and having no time for someone spurning the collection plate?

indicators.note: having no means the time abbreviation is taken out too
not removes the little word that follows from the clergyman

parts.note: a vicar is a minister of the church

explanation.surface: The vicar is out, and with no time to spare for anyone who won't put money in at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in' takes IN from MINISTER, and 'having no' time removes T as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-fisted hoarder would be expected to pass the plate on without giving, a playful illustration rather than a dictionary gloss.

clue.text: Intermittent springs? Small amount supplied without hesitation

parts.note: spas are mineral springs

indicators.note: without means the hesitation is removed from the small quantity

parts.note: a modicum is a small quantity
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Do mineral springs flow only now and then, delivering a little at once?
explanation.definitionFit: Spasmodic means occurring in fits and starts, at irregular intervals, rather than continuously.

clue.text: Disney film enthusiast sat up with Pixar regularly

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top
regularly takes every other letter, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A cinema fan sat up watching Pixar films time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SAT into TAS; 'regularly' takes I and A from Pixar.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is Disney's 1940 animated feature set to classical music, an example of the studio's films.

clue.text: Fool securing Times opening

indicators.note: the fool holds the multiplication word fast inside it

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person
by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: An idiot gets hold of a copy of The Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a deep chasm or gap in the ground, a yawning hole.

clue.text: Small quantity of salt, say, when eating a vegetable

indicators.note: eating means the letter is taken inside

parts.note: a pinch is a small amount of salt or a similar seasoning

explanation.surface: A little salt is sprinkled while a vegetable is being eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green plant eaten cooked or raw, a common vegetable.

clue.text: Way of training students variously in production of opera taking year

indicators.note: the learners are placed at different points within the mixture
a production reworks material, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a learner or student, so students give two of them

explanation.surface: Students put on an opera at various points in a show that takes a year to stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of' mixes the opera's letters, and 'variously in' places the two student Ls at separate points in the mix, an unusual way to clue two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Role-play is a training technique in which people act out situations to practise skills.

clue.text: Staff not left empty, given a meal

parts.note: a pole is a staff or stick

indicators.note: left empty means the inside letter is removed, leaving the outer pair

explanation.surface: The workers had nothing left, so were given a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees; it is a pole. 'meal' is cornmeal, not dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is coarse ground maize, a cornmeal, which is the sense of meal here.

clue.text: Understand end of austerity receives wonderful joy

indicators.note: the first pieces take the excellence mark inside them

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
A1 means first class, written with the letters AI

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Accepting that hard times are over brings marvellous happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) is written AI here, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaiety is light-hearted cheerfulness, a state of merriment.

clue.text: Gossiping, excluding source of latest fabrication?

indicators.note: excluding means that letter is left out of the gossip word

parts.note: tattling is idle gossiping or telling tales

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Chattering idly while leaving out where the newest made-up story came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding' removes L, the 'source of latest', from TATTLING. The definition is a pun: fabrication as making fabric, not lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatting is handmade lacework knotted with a shuttle, so it literally produces fabric, a fabric-making craft.

clue.text: Telegraph's leader bracketed by articles and letter

indicators.note: bracketed by means the two articles stand either side of the leading letter, like brackets

parts.note: the and a are the definite and indefinite articles

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: The Telegraph's editorial is surrounded by newspaper pieces and correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' and 'articles' look like journalism; they give T and THE, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: In Paris, the men from there used in support reflected difficult decision

indicators.note: the French pieces are put inside the reversed support
reflected means the support word is seen backwards, as in a mirror

parts.note: aid is help or support
le is the French masculine word for the
MM is the abbreviation for messieurs, French gentlemen

explanation.surface: In Paris, local men brought in as backing mirror a tough choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns the support word backwards (DIA), and 'used in' puts the French pieces inside it. MM, for messieurs, is the French counterpart of Messrs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a situation demanding a choice between equally unwelcome options, a hard choice.

clue.text: Is about to participate in party dancing

indicators.note: the pieces join in, going inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party
C is the abbreviation of circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to join in some dancing at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is a style of dancing to pop music in a club, so the noun names a kind of dance.

clue.text: Mixed messaging from the Italian Tourist Board?

definitions.text: Mixed messaging from the Italian Tourist Board?

parts.words: Mixed messaging from the Italian Tourist Board?
parts.note: the old saying urges visiting a southern Italian city before death, which reads oddly as tourism advertising, since it also invites the reader to die

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says a famous Italian bay city is so beautiful that once you have seen it you can die content; as an advert it seems to urge tourists to die.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying both recommends a visit and mentions death, so it sends a contradictory promotional message.

clue.text: A soft touch, Henry, gutless, showing disinclination to engage

parts.note: a pat is a light, gentle touch

indicators.note: gutless means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Henry is a pushover and a coward, too reluctant to get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' leaves only HY of Henry. 'soft touch' looks like a gullible person; here it is a light tap.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of interest or concern, which shows as unwillingness to get involved.

clue.text: Feasible to get support that's blocking of the Speaker in government

indicators.note: the feasible and support pieces sit inside, blocking the speaker's word

parts.note: my is what the speaker says of their own things
on means feasible or practicable, as in that's not on
an arch is a supporting structure

explanation.surface: The Speaker of the House is obstructed by a plausible prop in the running of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the Speaker' looks like the parliamentary officer; it simply means the speaker's own, MY.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy is a system of rule headed by a king or queen, one form of state rule.
